description: This schematic diagram illustrates the typical morphology of an estuary and its associated classification limits. The image shows green land flanking various water bodies. A winding light blue river originates from the right side of the diagram, flowing into a wider, light blue transitional zone that contains distinct greyish patches, indicative of tidal mud or sand flats. This transitional zone subsequently expands into a larger, dark blue body of water on the left, representing the open sea or ocean. Two prominent red lines are depicted across the water bodies. The lower red line crosses the river at its initial widening point, marking an upstream limit. The upper red line spans the wider estuarine area, signifying a seaward limit. These red lines represent demarcation boundaries for land cover classification, specifically distinguishing between river, estuary (such as CORINE Land Cover (CLC) class 8.2.2 Estuaries), and coastal waters (such as CLC class 8.4.1 Coastal waters), where the limit is based on the continuation of the coastline.
